title: Sample 17-13: Marked Intentional Spelling Errors

illustrates.quote: Marked Spelling Errors. When print calls attention to errors by means of a font attribute (e.g., underline, italics, color, highlighting, etc.) the designated words are uncontracted, and the remainder of the passage is contracted.

blocks.text: Read this narrative and rewrite the underlined words that have been spelled incorrectly.
Student 1: You know that new person in our `sceince` class? My `nieghbor` says he's the `hier` to a huge fortune!
Student 2: The `hier` to a huge fortune going to public school? That's hard to `beleive`. In fact, it's pretty `inconcievable`.

print.notes: Directions, then two 'Student' passages, each with several underlined misspelled words mixed into otherwise-contracted text — 17.10.3's own mixed uncontracted/contracted convention.
print.printFeatures: Misspelled words underlined; the rest of each passage in ordinary print.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between A and B; matches independent re-extraction exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged (both agreed '17.10.3', matches source). Modeled as three paragraphs; each marked-error word individually backtick-uncontracted inside otherwise-contracted running prose — the same mixed-passage mechanism standards-map.md (BANA 17.10.3) confirms 'done' via probe.
